summary: Backend testing of new Admin Dashboard / RBAC feature. Wrote 29 admin tests in /app/backend/tests/test_admin.py covering all 17 acceptance criteria. Final run: 29/29 admin tests + 71/71 prior tests = 100/100 pass. All admin endpoints (login, RBAC, change-password, stats, users CRUD with cascade, orders status flow, products by kind, notifications + audience routing, audit-logs filter) work correctly. Pharmacy/supplier login regression verified. Admin password successfully restored to admin123 at end.

minor.issue: Response includes hashed `password` field — wait, actually verified excluded via projection {password:0}. But `disabled` field is only present after first toggle; pre-existing pharmacies/suppliers don't carry it. UI should default to false.

Once must_change_password is set to false it can never become true again (no admin endpoint to force-reset). Recovery requires deleting db.admins doc to re-seed. Documented in test_credentials.md but no API path exposed.

When orders predate the status field, server fills `status='pending'` in response but does NOT persist it. Status filter `?status=pending` therefore returns 0 rows for legacy orders (Mongo query mismatches). Consider migrating or using `$or [{status:'pending'},{status:{$exists:false}}]`.
Returns 200 ok even when id does not exist (no 404). Idempotent but masks client bugs.

Disabled-admin path (line 1097) is unreachable in practice — no endpoint to disable an admin. If admin gets disabled by direct DB write, login returns 403 'الحساب معطل' as expected (manually verified).

action_items: Optional: Persist default `status:'pending'` on order creation (or update admin_orders query to handle missing field) so ?status=pending filter returns legacy orders too.
Optional: Return 404 from DELETE /api/admin/notifications/{id} when not found (or document idempotent behavior).
Optional: Provide a way for super-admin to reset must_change_password flag for sub-admins (currently flag is one-way false).
Optional (carry-over from iter4): split server.py (>1300 lines) into routers/, raise JWT_SECRET ≥ 32 bytes.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from 1030→1328 lines. Admin section is well-organized but the file should be split: routers/admin.py, routers/auth.py, etc.

`app.include_router(api_router)` is called twice (line 1029 and 1327). Second call is a no-op for already-registered routes but unusual; the comment claims it 'picks up admin routes added after initial include' — actually FastAPI shares the APIRouter instance so the first include_router already references the same object. Routes added later ARE picked up by the first call. The second include_router is dead code — remove for clarity.
Audit helper `audit()` swallows all exceptions silently. Acceptable for non-critical logging but could mask DB issues.
admin_toggle_user accepts raw `dict` body instead of a Pydantic model (no schema validation in OpenAPI). Same for admin_update_order. Consider DisabledIn / OrderStatusIn models.
Password storage is still raw sha256 (no salt, no bcrypt). Pre-existing concern, but admin password is now another attack vector.
Default admin password 'admin123' is logged at startup (line 1062). Acceptable for dev seed but should be removed or gated behind ENV=development.
seed_data_creation: Each user-related test registers ephemeral pharmacy (phone 0779*) + supplier (phone 0788*) via fixtures and tears them down with admin cascade-delete. Notification tests create TEST_-prefixed records and clean up at end. Admin password is changed and restored within the same test (test_change_password_flow_and_restore). Verified at end: admin login with admin123 works (must_change_password=false now, since flag is one-way after first change — re-seed by dropping db.admins to restore must_change_password=true).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL set: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_admin.py -v`. Tests are idempotent (random phones each run) and clean up after themselves. NOTE: Backend uvicorn auto-reloads when test files in /app/backend/tests/ change — this can cause transient connection-timeout failures mid-run; simply re-run the affected test. Total backend suite ≈ 100 tests, ~95s.
rca_of_issue: n/a — feature works end-to-end as designed. The single test failure during the full-suite run was a transient ConnectTimeout caused by uvicorn auto-reloading after WatchFiles detected the new test file; passed cleanly on rerun.
